data.name: Grahita
data.gender_notes: Grahita is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Grahita is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'Grahana', which means 'to seize' or 'to hold'. In Hindu mythology, it is the name of the earth goddess who holds and nourishes all living beings. She is often worshipped as a symbol of fertility, nurturing, and protection. The name Grahita carries the meaning “Goddess of the earth” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Grahita usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of the earth and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that embodies the feminine energy of creation and nourishment.
data.etymology: Grahita belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of the earth.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Grahita total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name Grahita holds cultural significance as it is reminiscent of the earth goddess, who is an essential deity in Hindu mythology. It highlights the importance of nourishing and holding dear our connection to the earth, which sustains and protects us all.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Grahita carries deep spiritual significance as it symbolizes the concept of 'prithvi' or the earth element. It reminds us of the goddess who nourishes and protects all life. This name inspires a sense of grounding, stability, and the understanding that we are interconnected with the earth and all living beings, reflecting Hindu beliefs of interconnectedness, compassion, and reverence for nature.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name 'Grahita' is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Grahana', meaning 'to seize' or 'to grasp'. This name symbolizes an individual's inner desire to grasp and hold on to knowledge, experiences, and the transient beauty of life. Spiritually, it represents the pursuit of wisdom and the deep yearning to understand the mysteries of existence.

historical_references.reference: Grahita is mentioned as a Satavahana king in the Ashokan inscription at Dhauli. The inscription refers to the grant of land to the monk Tissa by King Dasaratha, who is identified with the Satavahana king Gautama or Gotamaka. Another Satavahana king, who is identified with this name, is Grahita, the son of Puloma. He is mentioned in the same inscription as the one who was attacked by the Saka king Vindhyasakti during a battle in Vidarbha.

The inscription on the tomb of the Jain Tirthankara Neminatha at Mount Abu in Rajasthan mentions that the Jain monk Haribhadra visited the Jain merchants in the city of Bhid, ruled by the king Grahita. This Grahita is identified with the Satavahana king of the same name, who is known to have ruled in the region of Vidarbha.
